authority: CEO R331 Gate 5 — P-22 control loop model

control_loop_architecture.sensor: Distributed pressure sensors along catheter (measure local ICP gradient)
control_loop_architecture.state_estimator: Kalman filter estimating catheter position from pressure gradient measurements
control_loop_architecture.controller: PID or LQR controller computing required actuation force/direction
control_loop_architecture.actuator: SMP segments with thermal activation (shape-memory recovery)
control_loop_architecture.plant: Catheter in CSF space (bending, friction, tissue contact, buckling)
control_loop_architecture.disturbance: CSF flow pulsatility, patient movement, tissue deformation

stability_analysis.method: Linearized model around target position. State-space: x_dot = Ax + Bu + w
stability_analysis.A_matrix: Catheter bending dynamics (Euler-Bernoulli beam in CSF). A is stable if beam is straight (eigenvalues real, negative).
stability_analysis.B_matrix: SMP actuation force at segment locations. B is controllable if actuator locations span the mode shapes.
stability_analysis.C_matrix: Pressure sensor measurements. C is observable if sensor locations span mode shapes.

controllability.result: CONDITIONALLY CONTROLLABLE — if SMP segments are placed at mode-shape antinodes (every L/4), the system is controllable. If placed at nodes (L/2), it is NOT controllable.
controllability.implication: SMP segment PLACEMENT matters. Random placement may not yield controllability.

observability.result: CONDITIONALLY OBSERVABLE — pressure sensors must be at locations with nonzero pressure gradient. If all sensors are at zero-gradient points, system is unobservable.
observability.implication: Sensor PLACEMENT matters. Need ≥3 sensors at non-collinear positions.

delay.stability_impact: 30s delay is VERY LARGE for closed-loop control. Standard PID with 30s delay will be unstable unless controller is designed for delay (Smith predictor or model predictive control).
delay.finding: STABILITY CONCERN — 30s actuation delay makes standard feedback control unstable. Need predictive control (MPC or Smith predictor). This is a SIGNIFICANT engineering challenge.

buckling_interaction.finding: When the catheter buckles (Euler load exceeded), the linearized model breaks down. The system becomes NONLINEAR with discontinuous stiffness. Standard LQR/PID cannot handle this. Need nonlinear control (sliding mode or adaptive).
buckling_interaction.implication: Buckling + 30s delay + nonlinearity = CONTROL PROBLEM IS HARD. Not impossible, but requires advanced control theory beyond simple PID.

tissue_safety.rationale: Brain tissue is extremely soft (elastic modulus ~1 kPa). Forces above ~0.01 N can cause tissue damage. Our effective navigation force (0.039 N, buckling-limited) EXCEEDS the tissue safety threshold by ~4x.
tissue_safety.finding: TISSUE SAFETY CONCERN — effective navigation force (0.039 N) exceeds estimated tissue damage threshold (0.01 N) by 4x. The catheter could damage brain tissue during navigation.

failure_recovery.scenario: SMP actuator fails (thermal failure, material fatigue). Catheter is stuck in wrong position.
failure_recovery.recovery: No passive return mechanism. SMP is one-way (heated → recovers shape, but cooling does NOT reverse). Need bidirectional SMP or mechanical backup.
failure_recovery.finding: FAILURE RECOVERY NOT DESIGNED. Single-actuator failure leaves catheter in unknown position with no recovery.

verdict.control_stable: NOT PROVEN — 30s delay + buckling nonlinearity + tissue safety concern + no failure recovery
verdict.buckling_safe: NO — buckling limits effective force AND creates nonlinearity
verdict.tissue_safe: NO — effective force 4x above estimated damage threshold
verdict.label: T1 (COMPUTATIONALLY_SUPPORTED) — actuation hypothesis is plausible but control system has FOUR unresolved issues: (1) 30s delay stability, (2) buckling nonlinearity, (3) tissue safety, (4) failure recovery. NOT 'autonomous catheter navigation.'
verdict.next_action: COMMISSION computational: MPC design for delayed nonlinear system + tissue force constraint analysis. OR redesign with bidirectional SMP + force feedback.
